title: Sundial Systems - Console operational economics tour
summary: AE + SE walked Sundial Systems through Redwood Console focusing on per-route visibility, usage analytics, and cost decomposition for chargeback. Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted, SOC2/KMS, and a pilot to validate latency/cost claims. Agreed next steps: send pricing/pilot terms, share security pack, provision trial org and baseline dashboard for their traffic pattern.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lina (Sundial), Ravi (Sundial), Tara (Sundial)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick intro: I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, and Carlos is our systems engineer. Today we'll run through the Console — mostly per-route visibility, usage analytics, and how the cost breakdown can feed into your chargeback.

[00:35] Lina: Thanks, Maya. Quick context — we're building a multi-product assistant platform, lots of routes; finance wants per-team chargeback and ops needs latency SLOs. We're on AWS, mix of public and some private tenant data. Main ask is can you show us how we can attribute spend per route and tie it back to teams?

[01:10] Carlos (Redwood SE): Absolutely. I'll share my screen — starting with the Console home. Note: permissions on the left — RBAC — we'll show a Finance view versus Platform view. The key is route tagging: you can map routes to service owners and we stitch token-level usage to those tags.

[02:00] Carlos: (shows dashboard) Here is the Usage Overview — top panel is tokens per minute, then model mix, then route breakouts. We have the per-route card — click into "/chat/assistant" route and you see token distribution, median latency, and cost per 1k tokens. You'll also see anomaly flags if a route's average context length shifts — that's often a cost driver.

[03:15] Ravi: The context length anomaly thing — is that based on rolling 24 hours? We have some batch jobs that spike once a day and it skews our unit economics, wondering if we can exclude scheduled jobs.

[04:00] Carlos: Yes, the default window is 24 hours but you can change to custom windows and exclude specific routes or tags. Also we support sampling-based baselines so you can filter by traffic attribute — e.g., exclude 'batch' tag. There's also a prefix/KV cache metric — sometimes it's labeled "KV cash" in older exports — ignore that typo, it means KV cache hit rate which shows how much prefix reuse is saving tokens.

[06:30] Maya: Quick product note — Optimize will surface batching and quantization suggestions per route. For example, if /generate-summary has stable short context we might recommend int8 quantization and a smaller model variant to reduce cost by ~30% without visible quality loss.

[09:00] Tara (Finance): How deterministic are those savings? We need conservative numbers for budgeting. Finance will require a baseline and downside assumptions.

[12:20] Carlos: We provide both point estimates and 90% confidence ranges. For pilots we can run a simulated pass on historical traces (you can upload a day's traffic) and the Console will produce a projected cost delta between existing model config and recommended config. Results include latency percentiles so you can see tradeoffs.

[15:00] Lina: We have concerns about data residency and audits — SOC 2 reference is one, but also KMS for customer keys. Can we run the Console with a private control plane or VPC?

[18:10] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports a VPC-hosted control plane and on-prem options. We integrate KMS/HSM for key management and provide full audit logs. We'll attach the security pack after the call. Note the audit logs show per-token access and admin activity — that feeds into your compliance reports.

[22:00] Ravi: For latency-critical routes we may want Dedicated capacity — how does the Console show pre-warmed pools and tail latency?

[26:00] Carlos: In the model pool tab you can see capacity reservations and P50/P95/P99 latencies per pool. We also show throttles, queueing times, and how autoscaling influenced latency. For Dedicated you get guaranteed pool sizes — we surface expected queueing when you hit burst patterns.

[30:30] Lina: Walk me through a real chargeback example — finance wants to bill teams monthly by route. How granular can the billing export get?

[35:00] Carlos: Exports can be hourly, per-route, per-model, and include token counts, compute GPU seconds, and model variant used. You can push the export to S3 or BigQuery. There's also a pre-built billing mapping that maps route tags to ledger codes. We can show a sample CSV.

[38:20] Tara: Ok, that helps. A couple of practical questions — do you support SAML SSO, SCIM, and role provisioning? Also any limits on number of routes or tagging cardinality?

[41:10] Maya: Yes to SAML and SCIM; provisioning is standard. Tagging cardinality is very large — we’ve supported customers with tens of thousands of routes, but we usually recommend a hierarchical naming scheme to keep dashboards readable.

[41:30] Maya: Quick recap — we'll send: 1) tailored pricing and pilot terms, 2) security pack with SOC2/KMS detail, 3) a sample billing CSV exported from Console with a mock mapping for your routes, 4) a provisioned trial org with preloaded dashboard using a sanitized sample of your traffic if you share a day's traces. Any other items?

[41:50] Lina: That sounds good. Let's aim to kick off a pilot in early January. Finance will review pricing and if ok we'll commit to a 90-day pilot with a baseline benchmark run.

[42:05] Maya: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with next steps.

Notes on transcript quality: there are occasional mis-hearings (product names sometimes slightly wrong in auto-captions) and a few speaker attribution slips but overall medium fidelity.
